related_questions.question: What is the new treatment for macular degeneration?

text_blocks.snippet: New treatments for macular degeneration include both medications and novel therapies. For geographic atrophy (late-stage dry AMD), two FDA-approved medications, Syfovre (pegcetacoplan) and Izervay (avacincaptad pegol), are injected into the eye to slow down the progression of the disease. Additionally, a new non-invasive therapy called photobiomodulation (using light) has been approved for intermediate dry AMD, offering a way to improve vision earlier in the disease process.

list.title: Syfovre (pegcetacoplan) and Izervay (avacincaptad pegol):
list.snippet: These are the first FDA-approved medications specifically for geographic atrophy, a form of dry AMD. They are administered via intravitreal injection and work by targeting the complement system, which plays a role in the disease's progression.

list.title: Photobiomodulation (Valeda Light Delivery System):
list.snippet: This non-invasive therapy uses red and near-infrared light to stimulate cellular processes in the retina, potentially reducing inflammation and improving cell function. It is approved for intermediate dry AMD and can improve vision by more than 5 letters on an eye chart over 24 months, according to the Duke Department of Ophthalmology.

list.title: Anti-VEGF injections:
list.snippet: These remain a standard treatment for wet AMD, helping to reduce the growth of abnormal blood vessels and leakage.

list.title: Gene therapy:
list.snippet: This is an exciting area of research, with the potential to offer a more targeted and potentially longer-lasting treatment for wet AMD, according to the Norwood Park Eye Center.

list.title: Targeted retinal laser therapy:
list.snippet: This technique uses lasers to precisely seal leaking blood vessels, minimizing damage to surrounding tissue.

list.title: Thermal laser therapy:
list.snippet: This type of laser therapy aims to halt the growth of abnormal blood vessels.

list.title: Implantable Miniature Telescope (IMT):
list.snippet: A smaller version of the IMT, called the SING IMT™, is entering clinical trials, potentially offering improved precision and reduced surgical trauma for late-stage AMD.

list.title: Stem cell therapy:
list.snippet: This involves replacing damaged retinal cells with healthy, new cells derived from stem cells.

list.title: Topical treatments:
list.snippet: Researchers are exploring the development of eye drops that can reduce inflammation and protect retinal cells.

list.title: Oral medications:
list.snippet: Drugs like Duravyu (vorolanib), an oral anti-VEGF drug, are also in development, according to Verywell Health.

related_questions.question: What drugs can cause macular degeneration?

text_blocks.snippet: While no medications directly cause macular degeneration (AMD), some medications can increase the risk of developing AMD or worsen existing AMD. These include certain blood pressure medications, NSAIDs, hydroxychloroquine, and some medications used for diabetes and breast cancer treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: blood pressure medications, NSAIDs, hydroxychloroquine, and some medications used for diabetes and breast cancer treatment

text_blocks.snippet: Medications that may increase AMD risk or severity:

list.title: Blood Pressure Medications:
list.snippet: Some vasodilators, like Apresoline and Loniten, and beta-blockers have been associated with an increased risk of AMD, particularly wet AMD.

list.title: Nonsteroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs (NSAIDs):
list.snippet: Long-term use of NSAIDs, including aspirin, has been linked to a higher risk of developing wet AMD, according to a study from the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

list.title: Hydroxychloroquine:
list.snippet: This medication, used for autoimmune disorders, can cause retinal toxicity and vision loss, especially with long-term use and high doses.

list.title: Tamoxifen:
list.snippet: This breast cancer drug has been associated with an increased risk of developing AMD.

list.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists:
list.snippet: Some studies suggest a potential link between these diabetes and weight loss medications and an increased risk of wet AMD, especially with prolonged use.

list.title: Other Medications:
list.snippet: Some ocular antihypertensive eye drops, certain medications used for diabetes (like Actos), and even some birth control pills have also been associated with potential risks to eye health.

list.title: Individual Risk:
list.snippet: The risk of developing AMD due to medication use can vary based on individual factors like age, genetics, and overall health.

list.title: Consultation with a Doctor:
list.snippet: It's crucial to discuss any concerns about medication side effects with a doctor or ophthalmologist, especially if you have a history of AMD or other eye conditions.

list.title: Regular Eye Exams:
list.snippet: Regular eye exams are recommended for everyone, especially those taking medications that may affect vision, to monitor eye health and detect any potential problems early.
